Proof. Proof of q beta c k leading bias correction identity

Proof (one-line ring identity)

Substitute the bias hypothesis for both \hat c_k and \hat c_{k+1}:

\hat c_k^{\mathrm{corr}}
\;=\; \hat c_k - \hat c_{k+1} \cdot u_0
\;=\; (c_k^{\mathrm{alg}} + c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0)
    - (c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} + c_{k+2}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0) \cdot u_0
\;=\; c_k^{\mathrm{alg}} + c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0
    - c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0 - c_{k+2}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0^2
\;=\; c_k^{\mathrm{alg}} - c_{k+2}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0^2.

The cross-talk at order u_0^2 remains; modulo u_0^2, the bias-corrected value equals c_k^{\mathrm{alg}}. \blacksquare

canonical confirmation at q_0

The canonical evaluation the canonical formalism applies this identity to the SDP-extracted \hat c_k at the proton-pinned q_0:

Rung \hat c_k (SDP extracted) \hat c_k^{\mathrm{corr}} (this proposition) Algebraic target
k = 2 -1.0171 -0.9999932 -1 (canonical, prop:q-beta-c-2-eq-neg-one-structural)
k = 3 -2.0097 -1.9999968 -2 = J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(q=1)

The bias correction recovers the canonical c_2 = -1 to 7\,\mathrm{ppm} and the empirical near-match c_3 = -2 = J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(q=1) to 3\,\mathrm{ppm} — both within the O(u_0^2) residual predicted by this proposition (with u_0 \approx 0.00852, u_0^2 \approx 7.3 \times 10^{-5}).
